'''William Arthur Stein''' (born February 21, 1974) is an American [[software developer]] and previously a [[professor]] of [[mathematician|mathematics]] at the [[University of Washington]].

Stein received his PhD in 2000, from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], for his dissertation ‘Explicit Approaches to Modular Abelian Varieties’,<ref name="dissertation">{{cite web | last=Stein | first=William Arthur| title=Explicit approaches to modular abelian varieties | date=2000 | url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=a84086ae26381f0ebc20871e08201a0ceac8d027 | access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref> supervised by [[Hendrik Lenstra|Hendrik W. Lenstra]].

Stein is the lead developer of [[SageMath]] and founder of [[CoCalc]]. Stein does computational and theoretical research into the problem of [[computation|computing]] with [[modular form]]s and the [[Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward.do?AwardNumber=0555776|title = NSF Award Search: Award # 0555776 - Explicit Approaches to Modular Forms and Modular Abelian Varieties}}</ref> He is considered "a leading expert in the field of computational arithmetic".<ref>{{cite web|last=Kleinert|first=Werner|title=Zbl 1110.11015|url=http://www.zentralblatt-math.org/zbmath/search/?q=an%3A1110.11015|work=Zentralblatt MATH|accessdate=18 April 2012}}</ref>

Stein was the 2013 recipient<ref name="Jenks">{{cite web | title=2013 Richard D. Jenks Memorial Prize Award | website=SIGSAM Home Page | date=28 June 2013 | url=https://www.sigsam.org/awards/jenks/awardees/2013/ | access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref> of the Richard Dimick Jenks Memorial Prize Award, presented by [[SIGSAM]], a special interest group of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]].
